- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30%.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–25%.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00), especially in early forecast horizon — cap forecast values at 1.2x recent high or 1.5x recent mean.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 0.5x recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture short-term volatility — adjust for sentiment volatility: if sentiment swings >0.3, add 5–10% buffer to forecast extremes.
- When sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift direction.
- Avoid forecasting below 0.2x recent low unless sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and confirmed over 3+ days.
